q: 101. The area of the cross-section of a road fully in banking shown in figure is
explain: This formula represents the area of a trapezoidal cross-section in an embankment (banking) when the original ground has a transverse slope 'r' and the side slopes are 's'.

q: 102. Berms are provided in canals if these are
options: partly in excavation and partly in embankment
explain: Berms are horizontal ledges left between the top of the cutting and the toe of the bank. They are primarily used in canals that are partly in cutting and partly in filling to provide stability and space for future widening.

q: 103. The cross-sectional area of the embankment of a canal fully in embankment (figure) is
explain: The area for a canal embankment is the sum of the two trapezoidal banks: Area = 2 × [bh + sh²]. If the top widths are b1 and b2, the formula simplifies to (b1 + b2)h + 2sh² (or sh² per side).

q: 104. The following item of earth work is not measured separately
explain: Initial activities like surveying (setting out), clearing grass/bushes (site clearance), and leaving 'dead men' (mounds for check-measurement) are considered incidental and included in the main earthwork rate.

q: 105. The excavation exceeding 1.5 m in width and 10 sq. m in plan area with a depth not exceeding 30 cm, is termed as
explain: Surface excavation refers to the removal of the top layer of soil up to 30 cm depth over a large area, whereas surface dressing is limited to 15 cm depth.

q: 106. Pick up the excavation where measurements are made in square metres for payment
options: surface dressing up to 15 cm depths
surface excavating up to 30 cm depths
explain: Shallow excavations like surface dressing (15cm) and surface excavation (30cm) are paid by area (m²) because the depth is small and uniform.

q: 107. The cross-sections for a highway is taken at
options: right angle to the centre line
the starting and end points of the curves
explain: Standard highway surveying requires cross-sections at regular intervals (usually 30m), at critical curve points, and always perpendicular to the center line for accurate volume calculation.

q: 108. The diameter of a domestic sewer pipe laid at gradient 1 in 100 is recommended
explain: For a standard domestic house connection with a 1 in 100 slope, a 150 mm (6 inch) diameter pipe is the standard recommendation to prevent clogging.

q: 109. For 100 square metres of plastered surface, the quantity of lime required for one coat of white washing will be
explain: According to standard analysis of rates, approximately 10 kg of unslaked lime is required to white wash an area of 100 square metres for a single coat.

q: 110. Annual rent is generally fixed at
explain: In valuation, the gross annual rent of a property is typically estimated between 5% to 10% of the total capital cost of the building.

q: 111. Original cost of property minus depreciation is
explain: Book value is the amount shown in the account books after allowing for necessary depreciation year by year.

q: 112. In preparing cement concrete by volume the size of the wooden box used to measure sand aggregate is
explain: While a standard gauge box is often 35x25x40cm (to equal 1 bag of cement volume/0.035m³),

q: 113. As a rule of thumb percentage of steel in R.C.C. columns is taken as
explain: For columns, the steel reinforcement typically ranges from 0.8% to 6% of the gross cross-sectional area; 1-5% is a standard estimation range.

q: 114. In specification of earth work in foundation trenches, drains etc lift ordinarily specified is
explain: In earthwork, 'lift' refers to the vertical distance soil is moved. The standard initial lift included in the basic rate is 1.5 metres.

q: 115. The volume of cement required for 10 m³ of brickwork in 1 : 6 cement mortar is approximately equal to
explain: Mortar volume for 10m³ brickwork is ~3m³. For 1:6 mix, cement = 3 / (1+6) = 0.43m³ ie 3/7

q: 116. The chamber provided in long horizontal members to counteract the effects of deflection is
explain: Camber (or chamber as written) is provided in formwork for long-span beams (usually 1 in 250 of the span) so that the beam appears straight after the initial deflection occurs.

q: 117. The volume of coarse aggregate required to make 100 m³ of 1 : 2 : 4 concrete is
explain: Dry volume = 154m³. Coarse aggregate = 154 × (4/7) ≈ 88m³. Option 'a' is often used in simplified tables, but 88m³ is mathematically more precise.

q: 118. In the analysis of rates, the profit for the contractor is generally taken as
explain: Standard public works departments generally allow 10% of the total cost (labor + material) as the contractor's profit.

q: 119. The weight of 10 mm diameter mild steel rod per metre length is equal to
explain: Weight = D²/162. So, 10²/162 = 100/162 = 0.617 kg/m, rounded to 0.62 kg/m.

q: 120. The cross-sectional area of 16 mm steel bar is
121. The unit of measurement of coping is
explain: Coping is a protective cap on top of a wall. Since it has a uniform width and thickness, it is measured linearly in running metres (m).

q: 122. A document containing detailed description of all the items of work (but their quantities are not mentioned) together with their current rates is called
explain: The Schedule of Rates (SOR) is a list of all construction items with their standard unit rates, maintained by engineering departments for estimation purposes.

q: 123. The approximate cost of the complete labour as a percentage of the total cost of the building is
explain: In building construction, the cost distribution is roughly 75% for materials and 25% for labor.

q: 124. Working out the exact quantities of various items of work is
explain: Quantity surveying is the professional task of taking off and calculating the physical volumes/areas of work from drawings.

q: 125. The unit of supply of ordinary cement bag
explain: Cement is purchased and supplied in standard bags (units), so it is measured by Number (No.).

q: 126. The unit of measurement of brick work in flat soiling is
explain: Brick flat soling is a single layer of bricks laid on their flat side. Since the thickness is constant (the thickness of one brick), it is measured by the area covered in square metres (m²).

q: 127. The technique of finding the fair price of an existing building or property is known as
explain: Valuation is the art or process of determining the present-day value of a property, taking into account its age, condition, location, and market trends.

q: 128. The unit of measurement of steel work involving flats, angles, channels etc is
explain: Structural steel members like angles and channels are estimated and paid for by weight. For large-scale projects, the quintal (100 kg) is the standard unit of measurement.

q: 129. Revised estimate is warranted when the sanctions estimate exceeds, for whether reason, by more than
explain: Administrative and technical rules dictate that if the expenditure on a work is likely to exceed the original sanctioned amount by more than 5%, a revised estimate must be submitted for approval.

q: 130. Filling work in trenches shall be carried out in layers of thickness not more than
explain: To ensure proper compaction and prevent future settlement, backfilling in trenches should be done in layers not exceeding 20 cm (200 mm), with each layer watered and rammed.

q: 131. 1 Katha equals
explain: In the Nepalese land measurement system (Terai), 1 Katha is equivalent to 3645 square feet (or 20 Dhur).

q: 132. The plinth area of a building does not  includes
options: area of the walls at the floor level
internal shaft for sanitary installations up to 2 sq. m in area
explain: Plinth area is the built-up covered area of a building measured at the floor level of any storey. It includes the thickness of walls but excludes open areas like cantilevered porches.

q: 133. The contingency during preparation of estimate of any project in Nepalese context is limited to
explain: The standard allowance for unforeseen expenses (contingencies) in Nepal's public works estimation is 5% of the total estimated cost.

q: 134. The slope of the outlet of 'P trap' below the horizontal is kept
explain: A P-trap outlet is designed with a specific downward slope (usually around 14 degrees) to ensure efficient drainage and maintain the water seal.

q: 135. The concrete work for the following parts of the building of specified thickness is measured in square metres
explain: Damp Proof Course (D.P.C.) is measured in square metres because it is a thin layer with a specified thickness. Roof slabs and floors are typically measured in cubic metres unless they are very thin, but D.P.C. is the most standard answer here.

q: 136. When engineering departments undertake the works of other departments the amount charged towards design, supervision and execution etc., is called
explain: Centage charges (or supervision charges) are fees collected by a specialized department (like PWD) to cover the costs of planning and supervising a project for another department.

q: 137. The plan of a building is in the form of a rectangle with centre line dimensions of outer walls as 9.7 m x 14.7 m. The thickness of the wall in super structure is 0.30 m. Then its plinth area is
explain: Plinth area = (Length + width of wall) × (Width + width of wall). So, (14.7 + 0.3) × (9.7 + 0.3) = 15.0 × 10.0 = 150 m².

q: 138. The quantum of work of any item a skilled labour is supposed to turnout in a day is known as
explain: Task work (or out-turn) is the volume of work that an average skilled artisan can perform in an 8-hour workday.

q: 139. The density of cement is generally taken as
explain: The bulk density of ordinary Portland cement is approximately 1440 kg/m³, which is often rounded to 1500 kg/m³ for rough estimation.

q: 140. The weight of cement in one bag is
explain: By international and regional standards, one commercial bag of cement contains exactly 50 kg of the material.

q: 141. The head of the division of public works department is
explain: The Executive Engineer (EE) is the administrative and executive head of a Division in the PWD structure.

q: 142. In the rate analysis norms of Nepal, the provision for contractor's overhead cost is
explain: Nepal's norms allow for 15% to cover both the contractor's overhead expenses and their profit.

q: 143. The cost of machine is Rs. 50,000 with a useful life of 10 years. Its depreciated cost after 5 years, if the salvage value is Rs. 10,000 on straight line basis, will be
explain: Annual Depreciation = (50,000 - 10,000) / 10 = 4,000. Total depreciation after 5 years = 20,000. Depreciated cost = 50,000 - 20,000 = 30,000.

q: 144. The valuation of a building depends upon
explain: All these factors contribute to the final value: a durable structure, high-quality materials, and a functional design all increase a property's worth.

q: 145. The gradual reduction in value with age of a property is known as
explain: Depreciation is the loss in value of a property due to structural decay, wear and tear, and obsolescence over time.

q: 146. The valuation of a property is done when
options: owner of the property wants to sell it
municipal tax, wealth tax, estate duty etc. have to be fixed
insurance of the property has to be done
explain: Valuation is required for various purposes including buying/selling, taxation by authorities, and determining insurance premiums.

q: 147. The value of property that can be obtained at any particular time from the open market if the property is put for sale, is known as
explain: Market value is the highest price a property would bring in a competitive and open market under all conditions requisite to a fair sale.

q: 148. The set annual letting out value of a property, which is obtained after deduction the amount of yearly repairs from the gross income, is known as
explain: Rateable value is the net annual income of a property used by local authorities to calculate municipal taxes.

q: 149. Municipal taxes are assessed on percentage of the net income from the property and it varies from
explain: While it varies by municipality, a common range for property/municipal tax assessment is between 10% and 12% of the net annual value.

q: 150. Sludge from a septic tank should be removed in
explain: To maintain the efficiency of the biological process and prevent overflows, it is generally recommended to desludge a septic tank every 1 to 2 years.
